content: My mission in life is not merely to survive, but to thrive; and to do so with some passion, some compassion, some humor, and some style.
author: Maya Angelou
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Holding onto anger is like clutching a glowing coal with the intent of throwing it at someone else—you are the one who gets burned. Retaliation only ties you tighter to the person who harmed you.

Across his life and work, Maya Angelou saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Forgiveness and composure are not signs of weakness or giving someone a pass. They are acts of fierce self-preservation, cutting the emotional chain that allows another person's bad behavior to ruin your peace of mind.
reflectionPrompt: What bold or necessary step have you been putting off out of fear of judgment or failure?

practicalInsight: When someone triggers your temper today, take three slow breaths before responding. Do not give away your power for the sake of a quick comeback.
